title: Finite Frobenius digit obstruction or root after a uniformizer radical
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $R\subseteq S$ be an injective local map of complete discrete valuation rings of characteristic $p$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Suppose $t$ is a uniformizer of $R$, $s$ is a uniformizer of $S$, and $s^p=t$. For each $u\in R$, at least one of the following holds: there exist an integer $m\geq0$, elements $b_i\in R$ for $0\leq i<m$, and $b\in R$ such that $u=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}b_i^pt^i+bt^m$ and the residue of $b$ in $R/(t)$ is not a $p$th power; or there exists $w\in S$ with $w^p=u$.

source.place: Tag 09EY, lemma-purely-inseparable-case, successive residue-digit argument in the last two proof paragraphs. The complete-ring version and the precise root ring S are supplied by Q25; the printed final paragraph names an undefined B_1.

proof.text: If a finite expansion with nonpower final residue exists, the first alternative holds. Otherwise set $r_0=u$. Maintain the identity $u=\sum_{i<n}b_i^pt^i+r_nt^n$. It holds at $n=0$ with the empty sum. At every stage the residue of $r_n$ must be a $p$th power: otherwise this identity itself is a forbidden finite expansion with $m=n$ and $b=r_n$.

source.place: Tag 09EY, lemma-purely-inseparable-case, last two proof paragraphs; explicit complete-ring digit argument.

proof.text: Choose a residue root of $r_n$ and lift it through the quotient map to $b_n\in R$. Then $r_n-b_n^p\in(t)$, so choose $r_{n+1}\in R$ with $r_n=b_n^p+tr_{n+1}$. Substitution proves the maintained identity for $n+1$. Recursive choice gives the sequences for all $n\geq0$. This uses only the surjectivity and kernel of the quotient map and the definition of the principal ideal $(t)$; no coefficient-field section or perfectness assumption is needed.

source.place: Tag 09EY, lemma-purely-inseparable-case, last two proof paragraphs; explicit complete-ring digit argument.

proof.text: Inside $S$ put $w_n=\sum_{i<n}b_i s^i$. Since $w_{n+1}-w_n=b_ns^n$, the classes $w_n\bmod(s^n)$ form a compatible family in $\varprojlim_n S/(s^n)$. Indeed, for $j\geq n$ the difference $w_j-w_n=\sum_{n\leq i<j}b_is^i$ lies in $(s^n)$. As $s$ generates the maximal ideal and $S$ is complete, the bijective canonical map in the definition of adic completeness supplies $w\in S$ with $w-w_n\in(s^n)$ for every $n$.

source.place: Tag 09EY, lemma-purely-inseparable-case, last two proof paragraphs; explicit complete-ring digit argument.

proof.text: Frobenius is a ring homomorphism in characteristic $p$, hence $w_n^p=\sum_{i<n}b_i^ps^{pi}=\sum_{i<n}b_i^pt^i$ and $w^p-w_n^p=(w-w_n)^p\in(s^{pn})$. The maintained identity gives $u-w_n^p=r_nt^n=r_ns^{pn}$, so $w^p-u\in(s^{pn})$ for every $n$. For any $N\geq0$ take $n=N$; since $p\geq2$, $(s^{pn})\subseteq(s^N)$. Thus $w^p-u$ lies in $\bigcap_N(s^N)=0$, the separatedness included in completeness. Consequently $w^p=u$, the second alternative.

lean.statement: theorem exists_frobenius_digits_or_root (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [IsDiscreteValuationRing S] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) S] (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) [CharP R p] [CharP S p] (f : R →+* S) (hf : Function.Injective f) [IsLocalHom f] (t : R) (s : S) (ht : Irreducible t) (hs : Irreducible s) (hst : s ^ p = f t) (x : R) : (∃ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin m → R) (b : R), x = (∑ i : Fin m, c i ^ p * t ^ (i : ℕ)) + b * t ^ m ∧ ¬ ∃ z : R ⧸ Ideal.span ({t} : Set R), z ^ p = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span ({t} : Set R)) b) ∨ (∃ w : S, w ^ p = f x)
